runscript.name: Mi-17 twin-engine FGGearbox validation (steady state, both engines)
runscript.description:
Validates aircraft/mi17 (two TV3-117MT-equivalent turboprop_engine sides, mi17_main_engine_1/2, combined through the gearbox element named mi17-main-gearbox into the single mi17_main_rotor thruster) on feature/REQ-003-fggearbox. Same pattern as this repo's own scripts/test_gearbox_steadystate.xml (aircraft/gearbox_test), but against the real Mi-17 config instead of the throwaway fixture.
Starting both engines (propulsion/set-running=-1) triggers FGPropulsion::InitRunning(-1) -> SetEngineRunning() for both engines (which also forces full throttle) -> GetSteadyState(). What to check in the notified properties once settled:
- shaft-rpm should spin up under combined torque and stabilize (not diverge/oscillate) -- compare against nominal main rotor RPM x gearratio, i.e. 270 x 18.5 = ~4995, per mi17_main_rotor.xml (see its own comments; not asserted numerically here since the exact operating point depends on gearbox friction/load not modeled in these throwaway table values). - engine[0] and engine[1] output-torque-lbft should be approximately equal (both sides feed one shared shaft symmetrically) and non-zero -- unequal values would indicate the double-counting bug GetSteadyState() was fixed for (REQ-003 review MAJOR #1) has regressed. - engine[0]/thrust-lbs must NOT read as double the true combined single-rotor thrust -- there is exactly one physical main rotor. - one-engine-inoperative should read false/0 with both engines healthy; see test_mi17_gearbox_oei.xml for the failure case.
Collective is pinned flat (fcs/collective-cmd-norm=0 and the fcs/adj/collective-bias default of 0.15 rad zeroed too) throughout -- a ground run, not a flight test. This validates the gearbox/ propulsion mechanism in isolation from flight dynamics; without it, the engines now make enough power for an uncontrolled liftoff (thrust up to ~35000 lbs observed vs. this model's ~15000 lbs max weight) that couples into an unrelated ground-contact instability (*CRASH DETECTED* in the sim log) having nothing to do with the propulsion model itself.
